name: Sclerotinia Stem Rot
symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on stems Soft rot on stems near the soil line White cotton-like fungal growth on stems Black seed-like sclerotia inside or on infected stems Wilting and yellowing of leaves Plants collapsing due to stem decay
description: Sclerotinia stem rot is a fungal disease that attacks the stems of many crops. The fungus produces white cotton-like mold and black survival structures called sclerotia. Infected stems become soft, rot, and may cause the plant to collapse.
management: Rotate crops with non-host plants Improve plant spacing and airflow Remove and destroy infected plants Manage crop residue after harvest
prevention: Avoid dense planting Monitor crops regularly during cool and wet periods Use integrated disease management practices
